newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 1.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - CZECH REPUBLIC - AUG 1.

text.p: HOSPODARSKE NOVINY - Komercni banka has joined the ranks of institutions with rapidly declining profits. The Czech Republic's largest commercial bank yesterday announced an after tax profit of 1,639 billion crowns for the first half of 1997. This represents a 36 percent year-on-year decline.

- The government will scarcely be able to produce a balanced state budget. All indicators suggest that the IMF recommendation for a surplus comprising 2.5-3 percent of GDP will not be reached. The finance ministry does not expect a post-flood boom in the economy as a result of increased construction and other repair activity.
- Chemapol president Vaclav Junek criticised industry and trade minister Karel Kuhnl for opposing a proposed sale of tanks to Algeria. Junek argued that the ministry approved the sale earlier.

- The rating agency, Moody's has begun re-evaluating the credit rating of IPB bank following the government's sale of its stake in the bank to Nomura. According to Moody's the direction of the credit rating change is uncertain.
- Deputy finance minister responsible for taxation and customs, Jan Klak announced his resignation. His successor will be ODS member of parliament, Michal Frankl.

- The Blax Corporation, majority owner of Poldi Steel announced that it would be selling its 50.3 percent stake in the Czech steel maker. Tomas Pelikan of Mossei International Holding, which expressed interest in acquiring 49.7 percent of Poldi said that no agreement has been reached on the price of the shares.

- Insurance companies now have a clearer idea as to the cost of damage caused by flooding. Insurance experts are not ruling out that the damage may have reached 10 billion crowns. Insurance companies maintain that the floods will not endanger their financial stability thanks to Europe-wide reinsurance.

MLADA FRONTA - Severe flooding in Moravia and Eastern Bohemia could drive a number of small business into bankruptcy. Entrepreneurs regard the 300 million crowns provided by the government along with the 200 million crowns on reserve at the Ceskomoravska zarucni a rozvojova banka for supporting small businesses as a laughable amount.
- Commercial banks today will begin offering the sale of bonds issued by the government to raise capital for dealing with flood damage affecting one third of the country.

LIDOVE NOVINY - Domestic demand for machine tools is expected to decline year-on-year to 3.3 percent, with sales not excpected to exceed 147 million crowns. The report was released by the industry and trade ministry.

- The Chemapol Group announced that it expects a 1.3-1.5 billion loss on sales of 45 billion crowns for all of its subsidiaries during 1996. The conglomerate announced that a more accurate figure will be released within several days following a comprehensive audit being performed by Ernst & Young.

PRAVO - The Agricultural Chamber is demanding that rapid financial aid be provided to farmers affected by flooding. The chamber estimates damage to agricultural land to have reached 1.8 billion crowns.
